title: Candidate Architecture
description: Schema for a single architecture candidate produced by Phase 3 (Architecture Generation). Each candidate represents a distinct structural approach to fulfilling the intent. Multiple candidates are generated and evaluated before selection in Phase 4.

candidate_id.description: Unique identifier for this candidate within the project. Format: CAND-NNN.

thesis.description: A single sentence that captures the core architectural bet this candidate makes. This is the defining idea that differentiates it from other candidates.
examples: Event-sourced microservices with CQRS provide the strongest foundation for real-time multi-tenant collaboration at scale.
A modular monolith with clear bounded contexts minimizes operational complexity while preserving future decomposition options.

summary.description: A 2-5 sentence overview of the candidate architecture covering its major structural decisions, key technologies, and deployment model.

structural_bias.description: The primary architectural style or pattern family this candidate belongs to.

assumptions.description: Explicit assumptions this candidate makes about the environment, team, scale, or requirements. Each assumption is a risk if proven false.
examples: Team has experience operating Kubernetes in production
Peak concurrent users will not exceed 50,000 in the first 18 months
PostgreSQL can handle the write volume with proper partitioning

advantages.description: Specific advantages of this architectural approach relative to the project's intent and success model.

liabilities.description: Known weaknesses, risks, or costs of this architectural approach.

subsystems.description: The major subsystems (services, modules, or components) that compose this candidate architecture.

interfaces.description: The connections between subsystems — APIs, message queues, shared databases, file transfers, etc.

flows.description: Key runtime flows that illustrate how the system handles important scenarios end-to-end.

fitness_scores.description: Pre-evaluation fitness scores for this candidate, keyed by dimension name from the success model. These are preliminary estimates that get refined during the audit phase.

advantage.description: A specific advantage of the candidate architecture.

description.description: Clear explanation of the advantage and why it matters for this project.

dimensions_served.description: Which success model dimensions this advantage supports.

liability.description: A specific liability, risk, or weakness of the candidate architecture.

description.description: Clear explanation of the liability and its potential impact.

severity.description: How severe this liability is if it materializes.

mitigation.description: Known mitigation strategy, if one exists.

dimensions_threatened.description: Which success model dimensions this liability threatens.

subsystem.description: A major subsystem within the candidate architecture.

name.description: Short, descriptive name for the subsystem.

purpose.description: What this subsystem is responsible for. One sentence.

inputs.description: What this subsystem receives — data, events, commands, etc.

outputs.description: What this subsystem produces — responses, events, state changes, etc.

technology.description: Primary technology or runtime for this subsystem, if determined.

scaling_strategy.description: How this subsystem scales (horizontal, vertical, auto-scaling policy, etc.).

description.description: What data or commands flow across this interface.

synchronous.description: Whether this interface is synchronous (true) or asynchronous (false).

contract_defined.description: Whether a formal API contract (OpenAPI, protobuf, AsyncAPI) has been defined for this interface.

flow.description: An end-to-end runtime flow through the system for a key scenario.

triggers.description: What initiates this flow (user action, scheduled job, event, etc.).

steps.description: Ordered sequence of steps in this flow.

items.description: A single step: 'SubsystemA -> SubsystemB: description of action'.

error_path.description: What happens when this flow fails at any step.

latency_budget.description: Target end-to-end latency for this flow (e.g., '<200ms p99').
